items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: his hero was Big Jim Robinson, a New Orleans trombonist who passed away several years ago

ctx.x: All right. Well about that same time that I discovered Tommy Dorsey, there was a jazz band playing at a pizza parlor in Huntington Beach. And my brother-in-law, who is a very good trumpet player here on the west coast, he and I often remarked how our musical lives would be different had we not gotten to hear that band. It’s called the South Frisco Jazz Band. In fact, they’re here at the festival this week. Their personnel has changed a little bit over the years, but they were playing Friday and Saturday nights at…

Orleans jazz every Friday and Saturday night we’d go over there. And you’re talking about improvisation, we didn’t understand how they were playing all this music without having any notes in front of them you know? And little by little we got to know the guys in the band and I think they were amused that a bunch of high school kids would think so much of them to show up every weekend. And during their breaks they’d sit and talk with us. And I remember the trombonist, who now plays with one of the Preservation…
Talk about classic jazz, that’s classic. Tell us about some of your work with some of the famous big bands.
